The caller's own authorization-request inbox
get.description: Only ever the caller's own requests; there is no route that lists somebody else's.

post.summary: Ask a principal to authorize something
post.description: Addressed by the approver's inbox handle, never by a principal id: an unverifiable handle and a handle for a principal that must not be asked both answer 404, so nothing here confirms that an id exists. Honours Idempotency-Key.

404.description: not_found: the approver handle does not verify, or names a principal that must not be asked

get.summary: The caller's own inbox handle, to share with whoever may ask
get.description: The only place a handle comes from, so a caller can never obtain somebody else's.

get.summary: Read one authorization request
get.description: Readable by its approver and by its requester. Anyone else gets 404 rather than 403, so the id space is not enumerable.

get.summary: Poll for an answer, paced like a device flow

400.description: slow_down: polled faster than the given interval

post.summary: Approve, echoing the digest that was displayed
post.description: Only the approver may decide, and only with the stored requestDigest: a request that changed between being shown and being approved is refused rather than silently consented to.

post.summary: Refuse, echoing the digest that was displayed

get.summary: Resolve an interaction reference (ADR 0086 canonical link)
get.description: Unauthenticated: a camera, a wallet pass and a pasted link all arrive with nothing. Answers an InteractionSummary and records that somebody looked; scanning is never approving. A malformed reference, a forged MAC and an id that never existed are one 404 at one cost. Negotiates on Accept: application/json returns the summary, anything else returns a minimal HTML landing page.

200.description: Interaction summary, or the HTML landing page

get.summary: The approver's interaction inbox
get.description: A survey, not a presentation: listing does not move anything to awaiting_approval.

post.summary: Raise a cross-device interaction over a ceremony
post.description: The server derives the binding message from the authorization details and computes the request digest over both; neither is taken from the body. Honours Idempotency-Key. Cookie-authenticated browser mutations also require an allowed Origin header.

201.description: Interaction created; the reference is safe to print

404.description: interaction_not_found: the approver handle does not verify, or names a principal that must not be asked

409.description: interaction_already_live: one live interaction per ceremony

422.description: unsupported_kind, or an authorization detail that carries card data

get.summary: Open the question as its approver
get.description: The approver only; anyone else gets 404. Moves the interaction to awaiting_approval and records the approver. The fronted ceremony's subjectId is never returned.

post.summary: Approve, with a proof bound to the displayed digest
post.description: Both the echoed requestDigest and the proof's boundDigest must equal the stored digest: they come from different parties, and requiring both closes the gap between what a person read and what a credential signed over. verifiedAt is stamped from the server clock.

post.summary: Refuse, echoing the displayed digest
post.description: No proof is required — refusing only ever removes authority — but the echo still has to name this request, so a stale tab cannot deny the request that replaced it.

post.summary: Spend the approval, exactly once
post.description: The requester's route. A compare-and-set on the row version serializes two executors racing to spend one approval; the loser gets 409. Spending an interaction that carries no approval answers 401 approval_required — the caller is authenticated and is the right caller, and what is missing is the ceremony.

post.summary: Withdraw an interaction
post.description: Either the approver or the requester, and available from approved too: between approving and executing there is a window, and a user who reconsiders inside it must be able to close it.

get.summary: What this request will take to settle (ADR 0084)
get.description: Reason codes and policy digest, so an approval screen can say why an authenticator is being asked for. Approver only; anyone else gets 404.

post.summary: Mint a WebAuthn ceremony bound to one approval transaction
post.description: The challenge is bound to a digest over the request, the decision and the effective policy, so it cannot be spent on another request, the other decision, or under a policy that has since been tightened.

get.summary: Where the caller prefers to be interrupted

put.description: Stores the wish only. The intersection with policy, live bindings and configured adapters happens at routing time, so nothing here can widen what an operator allows.

get.summary: The route a prompt would actually take, and what was dropped
get.description: Includes the exclusion reason for every channel that did not survive the intersection, so a settings screen can be honest about unconfigured adapters and missing bindings.

post.summary: A provider callback (unauthenticated by design)
post.description: A provider cannot hold a bearer token, so this route is defended by a chain instead: provenance over the raw request bytes, a stable three-part provider identity resolved to a live binding, a durable replay ledger whose insert is the claim, and the same approval evaluator the in-app ceremony uses. Every outcome returns the same acknowledgement, so the route never reveals whether a request exists.

isFallback.description: True when the active project fell back to the personal default.

AuthorizationDetail.description: One RFC 9396 authorization_details entry. Extension members are preserved verbatim, because the digest is computed over the whole object.

requestDigest.description: The canonical hash of exactly what is being consented to. An executor recomputes it before running anything.

fields.description: Paths that failed validation. Never the values at them.

InteractionSubject.description: The ceremony this interaction fronts. Inbound only: subjectId never appears in a response, so a reference cannot be traded for the id of the row behind it.

approverRef.description: The approver's inbox handle from GET /v1/authorization-requests/inbox-ref. Not a principal id.

url.description: The canonical HTTPS short link, <publicUrl>/i/<ref>. Never a custom scheme.

bindingMessage.description: Derived from the authorization details, never supplied by the requester.

InteractionSummary.description: Everything the holder of a bare reference may learn. No requester, no binding message, no digest, no authorization details, no subject id.

InteractionDetail.description: The authenticated approver's view. The approval proof and the fronted ceremony's subjectId are absent by construction.

ApprovalProof.description: The verified approval, reduced: no assertion bytes, no verifiable presentation, no JOSE. verifiedAt is absent because the server stamps it.
